development_runs.design: First design: several positions could be opened on one market; divergence rule at 3 sigma over a window of 300 settled trades.
development_runs.what_happened: The regime world was HALTED by the circuit breaker (drawdown above 20%) and never PAUSED by the divergence rule. The null world was halted too. On the planted world the stake was stacked on the same market again and again: 1999 executions on 3797 candidates.
development_runs.led_to: One open position per market (a risk limit in the rule file), one side per market, the regime decided per market instead of per candidate.

development_runs.design: One open position per market. Regime world: edge 300000 ppm before the change, true probability 600000-850000 ppm, confidence 300000-450000 ppm. Divergence rule at 3 sigma, window 50, baseline at least 50 settled trades.
development_runs.what_happened: The regime world was still halted by the breaker before the divergence rule saw the change: two windows were checked and neither diverged; the median stake in that world was 281 basis points of equity.
development_runs.led_to: Smaller stakes in the regime world (confidence 150000-250000 ppm) and a try with more, shorter markets.

development_runs.design: Same off-plan corpus as run 003; divergence rule at 4 sigma, baseline at least 100 settled trades.
development_runs.what_happened: No false pause on the planted world; the regime world paused after the change. It worked, on a corpus the plan does not describe.
development_runs.led_to: Back to the plan's 400 markets of 10 to 15 candidates, with a regime world of under-priced favourites whose edge before the change is deliberately large, and the rule at 4 sigma, window 50, baseline 50.

development_runs.design: The design that ships: the plan's 400 markets per world, one open position per market, divergence rule at 4 sigma over 50 settled trades with a baseline of at least 50.

suite_runs.note: No suite was run once: dev and rehearsal three times, holdout and stress twice. Each new run followed a change of the code digest; the last was a fix to the order in which files are listed (it depended on the operating system). The numbers did not move; only code_sha256 did. The holdout and stress seeds are therefore not unseen: the unseen run is the blind one.

blind_run.note: Hand set: 30 candidates written once for both arms (make_inputs.py sha256 185408e3..., inputs frozen 2026-09-30T16:57:20Z, before any run and before reading engine code). Both arms refused the first file at load because line 19 repeated an identifier (arm A: 'hand candidate 19: duplicate candidate_id', exit 1, no result file; arm B harness: 'RUN FAILED: RunError: candidates.jsonl: missing or duplicate candidate_id 'EV-04'', exit 3). Nothing had been measured; the identifier of that line became EV-19 in both arms (fix_duplicate_id.py) and each command was run once more. Evaluator's own flaw, left as it is: the market of EV-29 resolves at t=200 and the candidate arrives at t=210, so EV-29 tests 'after the outcome' and not 'after the stop'. The message of the refusal does not start with 'REFUSED:' as the protocol says it would.
